title: Sheaf convolution on abelian varieties and convolution monodromy
summary: Construct the character-admissible quotient of perverse sheaves on an abelian variety and its arithmetic and geometric convolution groups. Compute smooth ample hypersurface dimensions and Hodge data, use microlocal factorization and exterior-weight counting to classify connected derived monodromy, and obtain generic and Galois-uniform product monodromy for families. The period-map application records the precise dimension and trace-compatibility obligations that its proof still needs.
readme:
# Sheaf convolution on abelian varieties and convolution monodromy

This roadmap develops the quotient convolution category, its cohomological fibre functors, and the geometric and arithmetic groups acting on smooth ample hypersurface cohomology. Microlocal cycles and a finite exterior-power counting problem lead to classical connected derived monodromy. Generic simultaneous twists, Frobenius transport and period detection supply the geometric inputs to the Lawrence–Venkatesh method. The final arithmetic finiteness argument belongs to MordellLawrenceVenkateshPartII.

The complete reader is [research/blueprint/readmes/SheafConvolutionOnAbelianVarieties.md](../readmes/SheafConvolutionOnAbelianVarieties.md). The planning pass covers every target in SC.0–SC.9. It is complete at target level, with named supplier requests and two proof gaps; it is neither a closed plan nor a formalisation claim. The surface period assertion has a separate Torelli route; its polarized comparison and relative universal property are precise supplier contracts.

stages.title: Characters, convolution and negligible objects
stages.description: Define Π(A), proper torsion cosets (including coupled-coordinate kernels), and origin-normalized rank-one character sheaves. Construct derived convolution with δ₀ unit and inversion–Verdier dual. Establish generic vanishing before using it to prove the Serre and thick tensor-ideal properties of Euler-negligible objects. Construct the exact perverse convolution quotient through the existing Serre localization and its Verdier comparison. Distinguish arbitrary exceptional translates from geometric-origin torsion translates.

stages.title: Twisted fibres and convolution groups
stages.description: Define character-admissible perverse objects by all geometric subquotients. Construct their exact faithful tensor fibre ωχ=H⁰(A,−⊗Lχ), identify dimension with Euler characteristic, and define the finite-type represented convolution group on one generator. Compare good characters through a tensor-isomorphism torsor up to inner conjugation. Identify Euler-one simple objects with rank-one skyscrapers.

stages.title: Arithmetic and geometric Tannaka groups
stages.description: Construct the geometrically semisimple arithmetic category and its geometric category of direct summands of arithmetic pullbacks. Establish 1→G_geo→G_ar→Gal_k^alg→1 as a group-scheme exact sequence, with the Galois term the Tannaka envelope of continuous representations. Prove origin-normalized Galois normalization and geometric base-extension comparison for a fixed tensor generator.

stages.title: Hypersurface Euler and Hodge data
stages.description: For smooth ample H⊂A of ambient dimension n≥2 compute d=[H]^n/n!>0, N=n!d, χ(H,Ω_H^q)=(−1)^(n−1−q)dA(n,q), and e_top(H)=(−1)^(n−1)N. Define K_H=i_*F[n−1] and its distinguished representation of dimension N. For a good finite-order torsion twist over a p-adic field establish native Hodge–Tate weights −q with multiplicities dA(n,q), without a good-reduction assumption.

stages.title: Microlocal structure and simple groups
stages.description: Construct the clean conormal cycle ring with multiplicities and the clean characteristic-cycle comparison. Use microlocal factorization to prove minuscule connected monodromy and, for n>2, simplicity modulo centre for any smooth ample divisor with trivial stabilizer, including nonsymmetric divisors. Import the full minuscule table and spin dimensions, eliminate the spin and exceptional dimensions using 6|N, and relate inversion to the SL, symplectic and orthogonal alternatives.

stages.title: Exterior-power counts and exceptional degrees
stages.description: Define finite exterior-power subset multiplicities and the positive Pell-pair recurrence P₀=(1,5), P_(j+1)=(b,4b+1−a), with normalized threefold degree D_j=binom(a+b,a)/6 for j≥1. Derive the integer-weight Hodge constraint with its central shift and complement normalization. Prove the extremal width equation, classify n=2 and n=3 counts, and exclude the row for n=4. The first exceptional degree is 8855 and its representation dimension is 53130.

stages.title: Eulerian exclusion and classical monodromy
stages.description: Establish both adjacent occupancy ratios and all five q=2 terms. Prove the proof-specific Eulerian comparisons using CA.2’s existing Eulerian family and bounds; exact cutoff and small-case certificates are gap G1. Exclude the first large-ratio regime, prove k<n, then exclude the second regime through the final q=6 coefficient contradiction. Deduce the exterior-power classification and classical normal subgroup theorem for n>2, with only the Pell degree exceptions when n=3.

stages.title: Generic twists in hypersurface families
stages.description: Prove rigidity of constant tensor constituents for a nonconstant-up-to-translation smooth ample family with trivial generic stabilizer and simple irreducible connected derived group. Establish the full product G^c on coordinate axes, relative generic vanishing with no constant invariant vectors, and a finite representation battery detecting product containment. Deduce generic simultaneous-twist monodromy containing (G*)^c normally in the direct sum of its distinguished actions, with higher direct images vanishing outside middle degree.

stages.title: Frobenius and Galois-uniform monodromy
stages.description: Prove Frobenius avoidance for finite-order characters of order prime to the good-reduction residue characteristic p, using prime-to-p Tate modules and Weil weights. Count ℓ-power characters avoiding every Galois/cyclotomic conjugate of a finite torsion-coset union. Combine these with generic big monodromy for a chosen order prime ℓ≠p to obtain all-conjugate uniform product monodromy; exponent tuples may depend on the conjugate. No all-p-primary avoidance theorem is claimed.

stages.title: Isogeny pullbacks and finite period detection
stages.description: On the smooth-divisor open of a fixed complete linear system |L|, construct polarized integral period maps for [m]⁻¹H and their deck-character decompositions. Plan the target that some such period map is quasi-finite for n≥2. Import CDK’s bounded-norm finite Hodge-locus theorem; use a separate Torelli/rigid-Hom argument for n=2 and record G3 for the higher-dimensional trace-compatible period relations. Fix Pic(A), not merely the Néron–Severi class, throughout.
